title: Puppify browser editor: real-photo cutout driven by real jumping-jacks video
license_scope: The three demonstration media files in this directory include adaptations of the credited source video and are supplied under CC BY-SA 4.0. This does not change the separate application source, runtime/model, or historical archive licenses.

app_inputs.changes: Decoded source frame 38, full 640 × 480 image including original black borders; no crop or retouch.
First 81 source video frames, containing frontal jumping jacks and ending upright before the burpee; re-encoded as H.264 baseline/yuv420p with audio removed. No resizing, cropping or retouching.
app_inputs.reproduction_command: ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel error -i jumping-jacks-burpees-original.webm -map 0:v:0 -frames:v 81 -an -c:v libx264 -profile:v baseline -level:v 3.0 -preset medium -crf 20 -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart -map_metadata -1 jumping-jacks-motion.mp4

recording.method: Playwright recording of the actual production-built application in a new anonymous Chrome context. The actual bundled MediaPipe model inferred the reference photo and successive frames of the real video. A passive worker observer recorded results; no vision outputs or interface were synthesized.
recording.graphics: Chrome launched with ANGLE SwiftShader flags; successful pose inference reported CPU delegate.
recording.network: All page runtime requests were restricted to a loopback production preview serving vendored assets; zero external requests were attempted.
changes: Selected an 8-second uninterrupted playback segment from the actual screen recording (7.08–15.08 seconds of a 16.08-second raw capture).
Cropped the recorded viewport to the visible editor workspace: x=51, y=0, width=1176, height=836; no UI was rearranged.
MP4: H.264, 25 fps, yuv420p, CRF 21, silent, faststart.
GIF: the same MP4 segment downscaled to 960×682, 8 fps, 80-color palette with Bayer dithering; repeats.
editor.png: an actual locator screenshot of the editor workspace after pausing real playback, rather than a generated interface.

observations.no_person_note: One initial video result at source time 0 had no person; subsequent genuine inference drove the displayed motion.
observations.scope: One adult actor, one indoor scene, with a reference photograph extracted from the same video. The source clip loops; model pose/mask errors and rigid-cutout artifacts remain visible. This is a functional demonstration without landmark/segmentation ground truth, not an accuracy, throughput, physical-device, Safari, or GPU benchmark.

visual_review: First, middle, and final MP4 frames and the GIF first frame were inspected against the actual editor screenshot. The photograph, source-video inset, and cutout stage remain visible, and arm/leg poses change during recorded playback.
